RNA-seq Quality Control (QC)

rna_qc.Rd

Performs comprehensive quality control (QC) on normalized RNA-seq data stored in the active rna_project. This function provides a structured overview of sample quality, expression distributions, and overall dataset consistency, helping identify technical artifacts and potential outliers before downstream analyses.

Usage

rna_qc(
  project,
  group_col = "Group",
  display_corr_values = FALSE,
  highlight_outliers = TRUE,
  cluster_rows = FALSE,
  cluster_cols = FALSE,
  plot = TRUE,
  save = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

rna_project object created by rna_project().

group_col

Character. Column in metadata indicating biological groups (default: "Group").

display_corr_values

Logical. If TRUE, overlays correlation coefficients on the heatmap (default: FALSE).

highlight_outliers

Logical. If TRUE, detects and highlights outlier samples based on library size (default: TRUE).

cluster_rows

Logical. Whether to cluster rows in the sample correlation heatmap (default: FALSE).

cluster_cols

Logical. Whether to cluster columns in the sample correlation heatmap (default: FALSE).

plot

Logical. If TRUE, generates diagnostic plots (default: TRUE).

save

Logical. Whether to store results in the active rna_project (default: TRUE).

Value

An object of class "rna_QC" containing:

data_ready

Expression matrix used for QC.

corr_matrix_samples

Sample-wise correlation matrix.

plot_density

Density plot of expression values (if plot = TRUE).

plot_expr_boxplot

Boxplot of expression distributions per sample.

plot_lib_boxplot

Barplot of library sizes per sample.

summary

List with basic QC metrics such as library size, genes detected, and identified outliers.

qc_metrics

Detailed QC metrics including library variation, correlation structure, and classification of dataset quality.

Details

This function evaluates RNA-seq data quality through multiple complementary perspectives:

1. Library size assessment

  • Computes total counts per sample

  • Identifies outliers using IQR-based thresholds

  • Calculates coefficient of variation (CV) across samples

2. Expression distribution

  • Boxplots reveal global expression differences between samples

  • Density plots highlight distribution shifts across groups

3. Sample correlation structure

  • Computes pairwise Pearson correlation between samples

  • Identifies low-correlation samples

  • Compares intra-group vs inter-group similarity

4. Biological signal evaluation

  • Estimates whether group structure is preserved in the data

  • Stronger intra-group than inter-group correlation suggests biological signal

5. Automated QC classification

  • Library quality (based on CV)

  • Correlation consistency

  • Overall dataset assessment with diagnostic flags

These metrics are summarized into an interpretable QC report, helping guide decisions such as removing samples, revisiting normalization, or proceeding with downstream analyses.

Interpretation guide

  • High-quality data: low library CV, high sample correlation, clear group structure

  • Potential issues:

    • High library size variation -> technical variability

    • Low correlation samples -> possible outliers or batch effects

    • Weak group separation -> low biological signal or noisy data

QC should always be interpreted in context: biological heterogeneity, experimental design, and normalization method can all influence these metrics.

Pipeline context

This function is typically used after rna_normalize().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Basic QC
rna_qc(project = my_project)

# QC with custom grouping
rna_qc(my_project,
       group_col = "Condition")

# Display correlation values and highlight structure
rna_qc(my_project,
       display_corr_values = TRUE)

# Disable plotting (metrics only)
rna_qc(my_project,
       plot = FALSE)

} # }
